title: Completed coefficient isomorphism fixed by residue projections
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l and a scheme X. Given IntegralLisseReductionEquivalence c [def-per-integral-lisse-reduction-data], there is an isomorphism from the continuous integral coefficient sheaf to the inverse limit of the constant positive quotient ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-adic-lisse-module]. Its nth projection is integralLisseReduction n followed by the inverse of c.finiteConstant n.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1) and (4), with Corollary 5.1.5 for classical finite local systems; the comparison maps are reduction, inverse limit and localization. Their pullback and coefficient-extension compatibilities use these same maps. Etale-local existence of lattices is cited separately as an existing DAG node.

proof.text: The supplied finite constant isomorphisms commute with adjacent reductions: apply sheafification hom extensionality and use their constant-section normalizations. Assemble them with NatTrans.ofOpSequence and NatIso.ofComponents.

The given continuous coefficient cone is limiting. Compare it with the limit of the finite diagram, and transport the latter limit along the natural isomorphism. The cone-point uniqueness and limMap_π equations give every prescribed residue projection.

lean.statement:
theorem completed_coefficient_iso_exists (c : IntegralLisseReductionEquivalence l E X) :
    ∃ e : lisseIntegerSheafSized l E X ≅ adicLisseCompletedRing X
      (Ideal.span ({Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E} :
        Set (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E))),
      ∀ n : ℕ, e.hom ≫ limit.π _ (op n) = integralLisseReduction l E X n ≫
        (c.finiteConstant n).inv
